one_line: Drought browning of an intact mesquite thicket below a stock tank; the whole scene browned the same way and 2023 1 m imagery shows no mark.
summary: before.png (autumn 2020) and after.png (autumn 2022) show the 74 m footprint on the south-east tip of a dense shrub thicket immediately downstream of a crescent-shaped earthen livestock tank; the dark vegetation finger is present in both composites and the whole 1.5 km scene is browner after. hires.png (Esri, 2023-04-21, a year after present_from) shows the box filled with intact shrub canopy cut by one thin pale NW-SE line, and wayback_strip.png shows that same thicket and line unchanged in every release from 2014-02 to 2026-08, so no clearing, pit, pad, scar or structure appeared. difference.png shows NDVI decrease across almost the entire panel, strongest on every vegetated drainage, with the box one of many browned patches; the only increase is a teal rim on the tank margin. The stored per-scene series gives inside-vs-ring NDVI correlation 0.966 over 31 scenes, an inside/ring ratio of 1.45 before and 1.31 after (ranges overlap), and inside re-greening to 0.351 on 2022-09-22; the footprint (0.3165 to 0.2248, x0.71) and surroundings (0.2004 to 0.1355, x0.68) fell in the same proportion. The panel (three sceptics, all refuted, high confidence) concluded the detector's absolute-NDVI step on late-April composites picked out the densest vegetation in a landscape-wide dry-season browning between a green April 2021 and a dry April 2022, with two sibling candidates 3.8 and 4.7 km away changing the same way that year; fire, earthwork and a processing artefact are excluded.
explanation: Drought-driven loss of dry-season foliage in a phreatophyte mesquite thicket growing below a man-made earthen stock tank (bordo), part of a landscape-wide 2022 browning in the Bolson de Mapimi. The detector compares late-April composites year to year and flagged the footprint because its baseline NDVI is the highest in the panel, so the largest absolute drop fell there; the relative change matches the surroundings (same x0.7 decline, inside/ring correlation 0.966) and the shrubs are intact and still green up every wet season. The Landsat confirmation is the same browning seen by a second optical sensor, not an independent surface event.
next_step: Re-run the step test on the inside/ring NDVI ratio across the 2018-2026 April composites: a ratio that stays near 1.3-1.5 and recovers in wetter springs confirms landscape browning. A CHIRPS or CONAGUA rainfall series for winter 2020-21 versus 2021-22 would confirm the wet-then-dry spring sequence. No sub-metre image of the onset window is needed, since the 2023-04-21 Esri picture already shows the thicket intact.
